chunks: From him, from Fadalah and Ibn Abi Umair, from Rifah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who performed Hajj on behalf of another person, and he had no wealth, and upon him is a vow to perform Hajj on foot. Does it suffice for him regarding his vow? He said, 'Yes.'
ai.seo_question: Does performing Hajj on behalf of another person count towards fulfilling a personal vow to perform Hajj on foot?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the flexibility of vow fulfillment (*nadr*) by accepting proxy Hajj (*hajj al-tamattu'*) as sufficient discharge for a vow to perform Hajj on foot, even when the vow-maker is poor. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic principle that the spiritual intent and completion of the ritual act can supersede the specific mode of travel prescribed in the vow, provided the obligation is met. It underscores the practical leniency (*rukhas*) in Shia fiqh regarding financial constraints and the validity of substituting one form of worship for another when necessary.
